A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SSI-Bench. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched despite changes to the title, terminology, and organization.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of 31 VLMs, human performance, thinking-setting experiments, and qualitative error analyses on SSI-Bench.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds a benchmark-expansion pilot, human resolution and expertise studies, and a cross-benchmark consistency analysis.

M1.justification: v2 Appendix E.6 introduces and pilots a semi-automatic construction extension: annotate additional candidates in existing images, sample candidate combinations, and review generated questions. The original benchmark construction, ranking formulation, and model inference procedures remain unchanged; renaming CMSR to SCSR does not itself change the method.

E1.justification: v2 Appendix F.5 adds human evaluators without engineering backgrounds, extending the evaluated population. The original structural domains and ten task categories remain unchanged. The expansion pilot reuses existing images and task definitions, while Table 10 compiles previously reported benchmark scores rather than establishing new original evaluations on those datasets.

E2.justification: The corresponding main comparisons retain the same 31 VLMs, random-ranking baseline, and human baseline. Added model analyses reuse existing models, including Gemini-3-Flash, GLM-4.6V, and InternVL3.5-241B-A28B in Table 6; no comparator algorithm is introduced or removed.

E3.justification: The main evaluation settings remain unchanged, but v2 adds substantial evaluation designs: 1,000 generated questions from 100 existing images, a 100-question comparison of 1920px and 512px human inputs, and a category-balanced 100-question expertise comparison with a brief non-expert introduction. These add controls and sampling procedures beyond v1's evaluation.

E4.justification: v2 adds analyses testing whether semi-automatic expansion preserves model rankings, image downsampling impairs human performance, engineering expertise is necessary, and model rankings agree with reported results on general spatial benchmarks (Tables 6, 7, 9, and 10). These substantially extend benchmark validation; the existing thinking and error analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v2 adds no repeated-run or seed disclosures, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures. The new studies report point accuracies, and the existing statistical descriptions and token-usage plots are retained.

E6.justification: The original taskwise, pairwise, and thinking-table values are unchanged. New generated-split averages are 35.3%, 22.6%, and 19.1% for Gemini-3-Flash, GLM-4.6V, and InternVL3.5-241B-A28B, respectively (Table 6); these concern different questions, not same-setting improvements. New human results are 92% versus 90% across resolutions and 92% versus 91% across backgrounds (Tables 7 and 9). Table 10 adds compiled cross-benchmark results.

T1.justification: The structural-state representation, feasible-set definition, ranking formulation, difficulty threshold, and metric equations are retained. Section 3.1 and Appendix C add qualitative constraint examples and explanations, without new mathematical definitions, formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: v2 explicitly positions SSI-Bench as assessing general spatial reasoning rather than specialized engineering expertise and as complementing scene-centric benchmarks. The central contributions, 1,000-question benchmark, 31-model evaluation, human–model gap, and limited thinking benefits remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands explanations of how structural constraints resolve ambiguity, why deterministic tie-breaking is used, and what the new validation studies imply about generality and input resolution. It qualifies cross-benchmark consistency as insufficient for a definitive correlation estimate. The limitations discussion now explains semi-automatic scaling while retaining the need for human review.

D1.justification: v2 documents candidate expansion, combination sampling, generated-question filtering, and sampling and briefing details for the new human studies. It also clarifies that constraints are implicit in scenes rather than symbolic model inputs. Existing hardware, evaluation framework, parsing rules, preprocessing, and data-release information are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds Spatial457 and OmniSpatial to distinguish broad scene-based evaluation from diagnostic spatial reasoning. Other citation changes include adding Enact, InteractComp, and 3DSRBench, removing the manifold-learning and DST-Part3D references, and replacing the space-frame reference. These refine positioning within a largely retained related-work discussion.

P1.justification: The abstract and central introduction paragraphs are extensively rewritten around ambiguity, structural constraints, and general spatial intelligence. The title and CMSR/SCSR terminology change throughout, dataset exposition is condensed and reorganized, and the appendices gain distinct sections for constraints, tie handling, expansion, and generality.

P2.justification: v1 Table 3 is split into v2's main-text taxonomy Table 1 and appendix statistics Table 5, while the category-distribution figure moves into the main text. v2 adds Tables 4, 6, 7, 9, and 10, revises Figure 1, and reformats appendix examples and error cases, substantially enlarging the latter. These are substantive display changes beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens the paper with targeted evidence addressing resolution, specialist knowledge, and scalability concerns, while clarifying constraints and improving access to the task taxonomy. The gains are limited by the pilot studies' scope and missing participant-count and uncertainty details. The original evaluations remain intact, supporting a clear but limited overall improvement.
